The draft says going from 45 to about 52 minutes is 'inside the 10 percent step', but that is about a 15% increase. The bigger jump is in the running itself: moving from short pulses to 2 min run / 1 min walk, then to 2 min run / 30 s walk on Saturday, multiplies the actual running load. For bone stress, that load matters more than total moving time. One change, either slightly longer sessions or a slightly longer run block, would have suited a week-2 bone return. Ines ran about 40 km a week before a stress reaction in the left shin and ten weeks off, and a physio has cleared Ines for walk-run three days a week, stopping if the shin aches. The goal is to run 30 minutes without walking by mid-October.
